firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
Hi Elan, thanks for the clear answers in the other clarification threads.

I have one question about the "unpublished" requirement.

Earlier this month I built a small benchmark on Kaggle Benchmarks and wrote a short blog post about it for a DEV.to community challenge. It tests whether coding models solve the specification or just make the example tests pass, using hidden tests and "poisoned" examples that contradict the spec. The main finding was that several models explicitly noted an example was wrong and then special-cased it anyway.

Benchmark: https://www.kaggle.com/benchmarks/shiroganemaji/passing-tests-vs-solving

For the Paper Track, I'd like to submit a substantially extended version: a new dataset focused on Gemma 4 and small local models, an agentic multi-file setting where the agent can run tests itself, conditions without any hint that examples may be wrong, and the dataset and tool released as a reusable resource. The earlier results would be cited as a pilot study, and the new work would be the paper's main contribution.

Would this count as original, unpublished research, given that the pilot results already appear in a blog post and a public Kaggle benchmark?

Thank you!
